subject: LuminaHealth trial: acceptance criteria, timeline & model choices
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@luminahealth.com>, Dr. Tom Bennett <t.bennett@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: LuminaHealth trial: acceptance criteria, timeline & model choices

Hi Sofia / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please confirm or flag any gaps.

Scope (what we agreed)
- 4-week trial (POC) to validate triage + short-note generation for outpatient referral summaries.
- Languages in scope: English + Spanish (phase 1). French optional for phase 2 if time permits.

Proposed success criteria (acceptance)
- Precision/recall on key-entity extraction >= 0.88 F1 on the eval test set.
- Short-note generation: clinicians rate output >= 4/5 for clinical usefulness on a 50-sample blind set.
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 380ms for single-turn inference under production-like load.

Model selection (trial config) — initial recommendation- Primary: Mistral-7B-v1 (instruction-tuned), quantized to FP4 for lower cost and latency.
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B-chat (q4f16) for edge cases where instruction fidelity or long-context behavior is needed.
- Fine-tuning / adapters: light few-shot instruction tuning on your de-identified notes for Spanish coverage.

Evaluation plan / owner map- Redwood to run model evals on the shared eval_test_set_v2.xlsx (attached) — metrics: extraction F1, generation ROUGE-L + clinician usefulness rating. (Owner: Dylan Brooks)
- Lumina to provide 200 de-identified examples and clinician raters for the usefulness ballot by Day 10. (Owner: Sofia)
- Redwood infra & SRE will provision a dedicated trial endpoint and monitor latency/cost. (Owner: Marcus Lin)

Timeline (target)
- Day 0 (today): Confirm SOW and test data access. I attached a draft SOW (Lumina_POC_SOW_v1.pdf).
- Day 3: Redwood gets eval dataset + initial config; infra spike to validate endpoints.
- Day 10: First evaluation pass + clinician rating round 1.
- Day 21–28: Iteration and final acceptance run; go/no-go decision by Lumina.

Open asks / next steps- Sofia: please confirm data delivery cadence and whether the de-id process will be handled by Lumina or you need our minimal guidance.
- Tom: any additional regulatory/residency constraints we need in the SOW (e.g., specific EU data center pinning)?
- Internal: Marcus/Dylan — can you validate the latency SLO above for Mistral-7B quantized at our expected request size (avg 200 tokens)?

Attachments: Lumina_POC_SOW_v1.pdf, eval_test_set_v2.xlsx (stubs).

Thanks — I’ll loop in legal if we get a quick green light on SOW.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: LuminaHealth trial: acceptance criteria, timeline & model choices

Thanks, Stephanie — helpful summary. Quick confirmations and a couple of asks from our side.

Confirmations
- We agree to the 4-week cadence and the acceptance criteria framework.
- We can deliver 200 de-identified examples; our data team needs a secure upload link and the minimal schema you expect.

Security / compliance asks
- Before we share data we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short statement on data residency (we prefer EU-hosted endpoints for patient-adjacent data). Can you confirm Redwood can pin the trial endpoint to an EU region?

Multilingual nuance
- Spanish is mandatory; clinicians also wonder whether model hallucination on medication names could be an issue. We’d like to see how the fallback model behaves on low-confidence spans.

SOW / timing
- We can sign a one-page SOW quickly if the legal terms are standard. If you can send the approved SOW by end of day we’ll try to turn it around by Friday.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the secure upload link and SOC2 note.

—
Sofia Alvarez

Subject: Re: LuminaHealth trial: acceptance criteria, timeline & model choices

Hi all — quick technical note and concrete eval plan. I’ll own the model evaluation and produce the first-pass report by Day 10. Notes below.

Model/runtime decisions (details)- Primary model: Mistral-7B-v1 (instruction-tuned). Rationale: best latency/cost balance for short-note generation with strong instruction-following.
- Quantization: FP4/INT4 where available (we’ve validated quality regression <1.5% on our internal clinical extraction tests).
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B-chat (q4f16). Use fallback rule when generation confidence < 0.6 or specialized extraction patterns fail.

Evaluation plan (what I’ll run)- Ingest eval_test_set_v2.xlsx (200 records): split 70/30 for tuning vs holdout.
- Extraction: compute entity-level precision/recall/F1 vs ground truth. Target F1 >= 0.88.
- Generation: ROUGE-L + clinician usefulness ballots (4/5 target). Also measure hallucination rate (named-entity hallucination).
- Multilingual checks: translate 40 Spanish samples to English and run round-trip fidelity + native Spanish runs.

Infra/config notes (to Marcus)- Expected avg request size: ~200 tokens output, 350 tokens input.
- Latency SLO target: p95 <= 380ms on EU single-tenant trial endpoint; request concurrent load ~12 qps for test harness.
- Cost estimate: using quantized Mistral-7B we project ~0.6x cost of baseline Llama-2-13B.

Attachments referenced: eval_test_set_v2.xlsx (I’ll upload to the Drive link Stephanie shared).

Next steps / deliverables- Today: Marcus to provision EU trial endpoint and confirm SOC2 / region pinning feasibility.
- By Day 3: I’ll upload the first config and run a smoke test.
- By Day 10: Evaluation report + clinician ballot summary.

I’ll include example inference config in the report, but a minimal runtime snippet for the team: 
redwood.api.generate --model "mistral-7b-v1-q4" --input-file eval_tuning.jsonl --max-tokens 220 --temperature 0.0 --timeout 12000
